title: Handoff Minimap — Rollout Chronicle and Compact Run Notes
content:
Purpose and scope
This document is a compact, portable handoff minimap for the upcoming staged rollout (June sprint lane). It bundles: a tight day-of timeline, a minimal smoke/checklist optimized for fast ops handoff, a short rollback matrix, and a draft of the release notes we will publish post-rollout. Use this as the single-page brief for the steward handoff and on-call watch.

Status notes (quick)
- Build: baked on 2026-06-01, tag: v2026.6.3-rc2
- Main risk surfaces: model routing policy change, traffic split plugin, and new batching heuristic.
- Canary window: 30 minutes at 1% traffic, followed by a 90-minute ramp to 10% if signals green.
- Rollout owner: Aisha Patel (primary), Jonas Rivera (backup).

Day-of condensed timeline (hour-by-hour compact)
T-120m (2h before cutover)
- Final smoke run on staging (see smoke checklist), confirm telemetry ingestion for new metrics.
- Confirm runbook open and paging paths tested.
- Slack channel ready: #ops-rollout (pinned messages: checklist, brief).

T-30m
- Post-smoke snapshot: capture sample traces, token-latency histogram, cost-estimate delta.
- Announce go/no-go 15m prior in #ops-rollout.
- Canaries created and pre-warmed.

T0 — Canary start
- Switch routing: 1% to new variant. Tag traffic in logs with rollout_id=R-2026-06A.
- Start 30m watch timer.

T+30m — Canary decision
- If signals green → ramp to 5% first, then 10% over 60–90m.
- If signals degraded → immediate ramp-down to 0% and failover to baseline variant. Begin rollback protocol.

T+120m — 10% steady state
- If steady for 60m, schedule next ramp (business decision) or hold and run extended sampling.

T+720m (end-of-day check)
- Finalize canary log bundle, tag all relevant PRs, and start release notes draft for customers.

Minimal smoke checklist (fast pass for steward)
- API health: /v1/health returns 200; tokenized throughput within 10% of baseline.
- Latency: P95 generation latency not exceeding baseline+80ms on canary nodes.
- Errors: 5xx rate under 0.05% across all routes.
- Model output sanity: run 6 golden prompts through canary model, verify no obvious regressions (QA quick pass).
- Autoscaling: scale-up event observed when load > 70% GPU utilization in synthetic spike test.
- Telemetry: rollout_id appears in traces, cost-per-token metric present, and kv-cache hit-rate visible.
- Circuit breakers: fallback route configured and tested (manual trigger).

Rollback matrix (compact)
- Trigger: sudden spike in 5xx (>=0.2% sustained for 5m) or P95 latency > baseline+250ms for 5m.
  Action: ramp to 0% immediately, open incident, re-route traffic to previous model.
- Trigger: degraded semantic quality on golden prompt test (3/6 prompts fail QA check).
  Action: pause rollout, collect evaluation artifacts, rollback if triage > 15m.
- Trigger: infra capacity shortfall (node OOMs or scheduler failures).
  Action: pause any further ramps, increase reserve capacity (ops), or rollback to stable capacity profile.

Communications quick templates
- Go announcement (ops channel): "Rolling R-2026-06A at 1% canary. Steward: @Aisha. Watchlist: latency, 5xx, kv-cache hit."
- Rollback announcement: "Rolling back R-2026-06A to stable baseline due to [short reason]. Re-routing traffic and opening incident JIRA-INC-xxxx."
- Customer-facing release note intro (draft): "Today we started a controlled rollout of several server-side improvements to our inference runtime. Expected improvements: more efficient batching and lower token latency for short-form responses. Rolling out gradually; no action needed from customers."

Observability signals (primary watchlist)
- Token generation P95 / P99 (global + per-region)
- 5xx rate and error fingerprint counts
- KV-cache hit rate and prefix cache eviction rate
- GPU util and scheduler queue length
- Cost-per-token (approximate) and tokens/sec per instance
- Golden prompt semantic drift score (automated quick-eval)

Ops play snippets (notes-to-self style)
- If latency rises but 5xx unchanged: check batching config change and sample trace for long scheduling gaps.
- If kv-cache hit rate drops: consider warming cache for heavy prefixes and pause further ramps.
- If region-specific degradation: isolate by region mapping in routing and revert regional variant only.

Release notes draft (short-form customer-facing)
Title: Incremental runtime improvements and routing stability enhancements — June 2026
What changed:
- Improved batch scheduling heuristic to reduce latency for short requests.
- Updated model routing policy to prefer lower-cost variants under heavy load.
- Telemetry: additional rollout_id trace tagging and new token-cost metric (for internal/external billing visibility).
Impact and rollout plan:
- Gradual rollout; most customers will see no interruption. We expect small latency reductions for short prompt patterns.
- If you notice sustained regressions, please open a support case and reference rollout_id R-2026-06A.

Post-roll tasks (first 24–48h)
- Capture artifact bundle (traces, sample responses, canary logs) and attach to JIRA-RELEASE-1223.
- Run extended QA suite overnight against 10% cohort and report semantic regressions.
- Fill final release notes with observed telemetry deltas and post the customer note.
- Retro prompt: short 30m postmortem within 48h, list root causes and follow-ups.

Open questions / tickets to resolve before final handoff
- Should we extend canary window to 60m for model routing changes? (PRIORITY: medium)
- Confirm capacity reserve for unexpected autoscaling during business peak (ticket: INFRA-847).
- Finalize customer-facing phrasing around cost metric rollout (product).

Quick links
- Build and tag: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/actions/489
- Canary dashboards: observability.redwood/dashboards/rollout-R-2026-06A
- Incident template: confluence.redwood/incidents/ops-template

Notes to incoming steward (short)
- Keep this doc open during watch, update the "status notes" block with any quick observations and time-stamped decisions. If you escalate to incident, attach the canary bundle and mark the decision timeline in JIRA.

-- end of minimap chronicle --
